answer.question: Can artificial turf be installed under a Fruit Cove oak?
answer.answer: Where Florida’s residential standard applies, turf inside a tree’s drip line needs certification from a certified arborist that the installation will not harm the tree. Otherwise, plan turf outside that line and retain suitable planting or mulch beneath the canopy.

blocks.h2: Decide the tree boundary before the turf boundary.
paras: Mark the drip line of mature trees before choosing the lawn or green outline. If you want turf inside it, obtain the required arborist certification first. A shaded patch is not automatically available for base preparation just because grass struggles there.
Keep roots, leaf cleanup and the route around the trees in the discussion. A green can use the clearer part of the yard while a pet area stays conveniently near the door.

blocks.h2: Leave shoreline and service access available.
paras: For a lot near Julington Creek, Durbin Creek or the river, bring the shoreline and drainage information you have. The applicable state standard includes waterbody separation and keeps turf out of swales and ditches. Confirm those boundaries before extending turf toward the water.

On an older septic-served property, keep tank access available and obtain advice before preparation near system components. For a golf-facing or association property, get the current landscape requirements rather than assuming a backyard is out of view or exempt from review.
